comment: Pinned third-party investigation tools. Exact commits; fetch with toolkit/fetch_upstreams.py (verifies the checked-out SHA). Integration levels are explained in docs/modules/INVESTIGATE.md. 'reviewed' is the UTC date the upstream and its license were checked.
fork_policy: No forks: Umbra changes none of these projects' code. They are used unmodified (pinned), run in isolated containers, or exchanged through files. A fork is created only when a real patch is needed.

upstreams.name: tor
upstreams.how: Umbra runs the tor binary shipped inside the signed Tor Browser bundle (upstream/tor-browser.lock.json); the toolkit tor container uses Debian's packaged tor. This pin is a source reference for audits, not a separate build.
upstreams.note: Requested URL github.com/torproject/tor is a retired mirror (README says the project moved to gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/core/tor); pinned the canonical repository.

upstreams.name: tor-browser
upstreams.how: Umbra is built from the signed Tor Browser 16.0.1 release. This commit equals SourceStamp in the shipped platform.ini (checked by tests/unit/test_upstreams_lock.py against a built bundle).

upstreams.name: torbot
upstreams.how: Git submodule vendor/torbot (added by the project owner). Runs only in the isolated toolkit container through tor; its output can be imported as manual leads in Umbra Investigate.

upstreams.name: onionscan
upstreams.how: Scanner for onion services you operate or are authorised to assess. Isolated container through tor; JSON output can be attached to a case with tools/investigate/attach.py.

upstreams.name: onionscout
upstreams.how: Same model as onionscan: authorised targets only, isolated container, output attachable to a case.

upstreams.name: onionsearch
upstreams.how: Metasearch over onion search engines, isolated container through tor. Its CSV output is imported by Umbra Investigate as a list of onion leads that the user opens manually.

upstreams.name: ahmia-site
upstreams.how: Umbra Investigate offers Ahmia's onion service (juhanurmihxlp77nkq76byazcldy2hlmovfu2epvl5ankdibsot4csyd.onion, as published on ahmia.fi) as a search engine. Umbra does not self-host Ahmia.
upstreams.note: Requested URL github.com/ahmia/ahmia returns 404; the Ahmia project is split into ahmia-site, ahmia-crawler and ahmia-index (all pinned).

upstreams.name: ahmia-crawler
upstreams.how: Pinned for self-hosting Ahmia; not run by Umbra.

upstreams.name: ahmia-index
upstreams.how: Pinned for self-hosting Ahmia; not run by Umbra.

upstreams.name: ail-framework
upstreams.how: Large server platform (Redis/Kvrocks, crawlers, web UI). Run it separately on its own host; Umbra's Timesketch/JSONL and HAR exports can be handed to it manually. Not bundled or containerised by Umbra.

upstreams.name: darkdump
upstreams.how: Isolated container through tor; onion URLs in its output can be imported as manual leads.

upstreams.name: darkspider
upstreams.how: Not wired into compose until the owner confirms this is the intended project.
upstreams.note: Requested URL github.com/N0rz3/DarkSpider returns 404 (N0rz3 has no such repository). PROxZIMA/DarkSpider is the best-known project with that name; pinned as a candidate only.

upstreams.name: mitmproxy
upstreams.how: Umbra Investigate exports HAR 1.2; CI loads it with mitmproxy's own reader (mitmproxy.io.read_flows_from_paths) in tests/investigate. Live interception inside the investigate instance is deliberately not done (it would require trusting a MITM CA and breaks Tor Browser's certificate model).

upstreams.name: zaproxy
upstreams.how: Isolated container on the tor-only network, passive analysis of an imported HAR by default (HAR import is a ZAP feature). Active scanning is only for systems you are authorised to test.

upstreams.name: owasp-ptk-site
upstreams.how: This is the OWASP project website (no license file). The extension source it links to is pinned separately as owasp-ptk.
upstreams.note: No license file in the website repository; nothing from it is copied.

upstreams.name: owasp-ptk
upstreams.how: A browser extension. Not bundled: adding extensions changes Umbra's fingerprint relative to Tor Browser. Use it in a separate, non-Umbra testing profile against systems you are authorised to test.

upstreams.name: timesketch
upstreams.how: Umbra writes Timesketch JSONL (message, datetime, timestamp_desc + attributes). The schema is tested in CI; importing into a live Timesketch server is not tested in CI.

upstreams.name: plaso
upstreams.how: Run separately on case folders or disk images. Umbra's case log is already a timeline, so Plaso is not needed for Umbra's own evidence.

upstreams.name: autopsy
upstreams.how: Desktop forensics suite. Add an Umbra case folder as a 'Logical Files' data source; hashes in manifest.json/hashdeep.txt can be compared there.

upstreams.name: sleuthkit
upstreams.license: IPL-1.0 AND CPL-1.0 AND GPL-2.0-or-later (per licenses/README.md)
upstreams.how: Disk-image forensics library and tools; not relevant to browser-captured artifacts, kept standalone.

upstreams.name: exiftool
upstreams.how: tools/investigate/analyze_case.py runs exiftool (offline, in the network-less analysis container or locally) on captured artifacts and adds its JSON output to the case with hashes. Tested in CI.
upstreams.note: README: 'same terms as Perl itself (either the Perl Artistic License or GPL)'. GitHub detects the LICENSE file as GPL-3.0.

upstreams.name: hashdeep
upstreams.how: Every case gets hashdeep.txt (HASHDEEP-1.0, size+sha256). CI audits it with the real hashdeep binary (hashdeep -a -k).
